clue.text: In France, well cooked snail (blooming things they are !)

parts.note: the French word for well is bien

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A French gourmet admires a well-cooked snail, with a wry aside about flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges SNAIL into NIALS, which follows BIEN. The parenthesis 'they are' just points out that the definition names plants that flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that live two years and flower in the second are a gardener's classic flowering group.

clue.text: Mouldings for gems

explanation.surface: Decorative mouldings set with precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: small convex architectural mouldings, and narrow oblong-cut jewels.

clue.text: A human failing

parts.note: the proverb says to err is human, so a typically human failing is a mistake

explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is the archetypal human slip, as in the saying that to err is human.

clue.text: Ned captures new 11 with his lower charges …

indicators.note: one name capturing something holds it inside, so these letters sit within the name

parts.note: taken as the name as written

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters of the cross-referenced word are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, the four-cornered globe, our planet

explanation.surface: A man called Ned rounds up a fresh planet, then heads off with his cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges EARTH (11 across) into ATHER, which 'captures' places inside NED. 'Lower' is one who lows, i.e. a cow, not 'more low'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a cowherd: his charges are cattle, creatures that low.

clue.text: … one of them longing to return under the tree

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece under another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for longing is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: Continuing the cowherd story, one of the herd pines to get back beneath the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns YEN into NEY, placed 'under' ALDER. 'one of them' follows on from 3 down: one of the herdsman's cattle. ALDERNEY is a Channel Island that gave its name to a breed of dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dairy cow from the Channel Islands, so one of the cowherd's cattle.

clue.text: Gray cat finding one meal's elusive

indicators.note: something elusive slips out of place, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
read as the plural meals, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A grey cat finds that its dinner keeps escaping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elusive' rearranges I and MEALS. Thomas Gray wrote an ode on his friend Walpole's cat, drowned in a tub of goldfish; the cat's name was Selima, so 'Gray' is the poet, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat drowned in a goldfish tub in Thomas Gray's well-known ode bore this name.

clue.text: Border troop movement

explanation.surface: Soldiers advancing towards a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a frontier region (the Welsh Marches), and also a military walk in step.

clue.text: As a horseman he's told the silliest things

definitions.text: As a horseman he's told the silliest things

parts.words: As a horseman he's told the silliest things
parts.note: the old scornful phrase 'tell that to the horse ...' answers a tall story; a mounted seagoing soldier is the absurd figure

explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing soldier; 'horse marines' were a joke corps, the people to whom unbelievable tales are told.

clue.text: Argument about a relative over gin cocktail

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier piece sits over the later one

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
a son is a family relative

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A family row about a relative breaks out over a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING, which comes below RE, A and SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is a line of logical argument set out to prove a point.

clue.text: Clad like Pantaloon in garments — outsize he'd found out

indicators.note: letters put out of place are disordered, so these are rearranged

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The comic old man of the pantomime finds his clothes are too big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OS and HED; 'found' is a link. Pantaloon, the old man of commedia dell'arte and the English harlequinade, wore tight hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing hose, the tight leggings of the old stage Pantaloon, who gave his name to trousers.

clue.text: Navy's part in protection of fish

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a guard is protection
RN, the Royal Navy, is the abbreviated part of the name

explanation.surface: Part of the fleet is deployed to protect fishing stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gurnard is a spiny bottom-feeding sea fish with a large armoured head.

clue.text: Picketing ropes broken at rails

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Pickets' ropes have been snapped against the railings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picketing' here means tethering an animal to a picket or stake, not striking workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassos double as tethers for grazing horses tied to a stake.

clue.text: Four-cornered globe

parts.note: the phrase 'the four corners of' our planet gives a round world corners, a deliberate paradox

explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is a globe, yet we speak of the four corners of it.

clue.text: Via a proverbial long lane ?

explanation.surface: Taking a route along a lane famous for its length.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin via is a road, as in Roman roads such as the Via Appia; Roman roads were famously straight, and the proverb says it is a long lane that has no turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: Latin for road, and the straight Roman highway that never turns.

clue.text: Local man, say, in rent setback …

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
a word set back is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
to aver is to say firmly

explanation.surface: A local man is said to be behind with the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns RENT into TNER; AVER goes 'in' it. 'Local' is a pub, so its man keeps an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper of an inn, the local in British slang for one's nearest pub.

clue.text: Strange facet, love, shown by this turn-around

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd side of love is shown by this sudden change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had stray words after it; the page prints no more than this.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, from the French for turn face.

clue.text: … but could succeed, note, selling this

parts.note: to win is to succeed
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Continuing from 13: the landlord could do well out of what he sells.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 13 across: the definition is what the innkeeper sells.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is a staple sold by an innkeeper, the subject of the previous clue.

clue.text: Maybe fifty men, or ten, joining the services

indicators.note: maybe signals a possible arrangement, so the letters may be put into another order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Perhaps fifty, or only ten, men sign up for the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlistment is the act of signing up for the armed forces.

clue.text: Prone to 2

parts.note: 2 down is a mistake, so this describes being liable to make mistakes

explanation.definitionFit: Liable to err, i.e. capable of making mistakes.

clue.text: Botanist takes the odd ale with us outside the pub

indicators.note: a piece outside another wraps around it
odd means peculiar, so these letters are arranged peculiarly

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A plant scientist drinks a strange ale with us outside the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ALE and US into LAEUS, which goes 'outside' INN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish naturalist who devised the two-part Latin naming of plants.

clue.text: Make this deception acceptable

parts.note: one word means both a hoax and to win acceptance for something, so the clue joins the two senses

explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is an old meaning, and persuading people to accept something is a modern one.

clue.text: Well, don't go to work!

parts.note: someone perfectly healthy who still stays home is faking illness

explanation.definitionFit: To feign sickness to dodge duty, though in fact being quite healthy.

clue.text: Miss J. Boot?

explanation.surface: A young lady called J. and her footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain jemimas were elastic-sided boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name beginning with J, and an old term for an elastic-sided boot.

clue.text: Not fast, the girl I go wild with in the bar

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: letters that go wild are scrambled, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow evening: the girl and I let loose together in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges I GO into GIO after ADA. 'with in the bar' sets the musical scene: the tempo marking appears in a bar of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning slow and leisurely.

clue.text: In advance, give a pound of the cleric's pay

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before, in advance
to give is to bend or yield
L, from libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A vicar's stipend is paid up front, a pound at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebend is a canon's stipend, so this adjective relates to that clerical income.

clue.text: Small business in a hole, on edge

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a pit is a hole
CO, short for company, is a business in small form

explanation.surface: A small firm is in trouble and everyone is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny loop of thread worked along the border of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Boy backward for example in nothing, but gets confused in 20

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: read backward means written from right to left

explanation.surface: A shy boy turns out to be nothing special and gets muddled at 20.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns EG into GE, set 'in' NIL. The tail adds that the name's letters can be found jumbled in MALINGER (20 across).
explanation.definitionFit: A common British boy's name.

clue.text: Is such a viable concern on the way out?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a healthy business is actually closing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'going concern' is a solvent business, and something on its way out is leaving.

clue.text: Decorative pursuit

explanation.surface: An ornamental hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is ornamental engraving on metal, and also a hunt after a quarry.

clue.text: The 12 of the 'insect world?

parts.note: the straight Roman highway of 12 across, translated to the direct flight path of an insect heading home

explanation.definitionFit: A straight course, like a honeybee flying directly back to its hive.

clue.text: Second letter from Athens

parts.note: a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one a scientist uses for a second variable angle after alpha

explanation.definitionFit: The eighth character of the Greek alphabet, commonly used for an angle.

clue.text: Supervision, or 2 from lack of it

explanation.surface: Mistakes come from too little supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: watchful superintendence, and a slip made through failing to notice.
